name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Overlooks Tawang Chu valley with a 28-foot gilded Buddha, ancient manuscripts, and about 500 monks of the Gelug school. Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama; major pilgrimage site.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Houses 28-ft gilded Buddha and rare manuscripts

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m (13,700 ft) on the Tawang–West Kameng border, the gateway to Tawang on NH-13. Features Sela Lake (Paradise Lake), often frozen, snow-covered peaks, and the nearby Sela Tunnel for all-weather access. Iconic Himalayan scenery.
facts: Sela Tunnel opened for year-round connectivity

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake at about 3,708 m on the road to Bum La, formed by earthquake with dead tree trunks rising from the water. Popularly called Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film shoot; serene alpine setting with mountain views. Special permits required.
facts: Formed by earthquake (trees still standing in water)
Popular name from Madhuri Dixit film shoot
Army permit needed; near Bum La route

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular 100 m high waterfall near Jang town on the Nuranang Chu, about 40 km from Tawang. Originates from Sela Pass slopes; small hydel plant at base. Also known as Bong Bong Falls; accessible from the highway.
facts: Near Jang town, ~40 km from Tawang
Also called Jang or Bong Bong Falls
Small hydel plant at base for local power
On Nuranang Chu from Sela slopes

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4,600 m (15,200 ft) on the India-China frontier, 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade route and 1962 war site; Border Personnel Meeting Point. Requires special Army and DC permits; dramatic barren high-altitude landscape.
facts: Historic 1962 war route and Dalai Lama path
Special Army/DC permits required for Indians

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Founded around 1489 by Urgen Sangpo; smaller, peaceful Nyingma-linked site near Tawang with traditional architecture and prayer flags.
facts: Peaceful smaller monastery near main Tawang Gompa

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: 40-foot-high stupa-style memorial near Tawang town honouring Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features names of martyrs, light-and-sound elements, and views over the valley; maintained as a site of respect.
facts: ~40 ft stupa dedicated to 1962 war heroes

name: Jaswant Garh Memorial
description: War memorial on NH-13 near Nuranang/Jang honouring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles, who fought heroically in the 1962 Battle of Nuranang and received the Maha Vir Chakra posthumously. Maintained by the Army with personal effects and tribute rituals.
facts: Honours Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, MVC

name: Pankang Teng Tso
description: High-altitude lake near Tawang on the route toward Bum La, known for its serene alpine setting amid snow peaks and meadows. One of several sacred lakes in the region; accessible with permits depending on conditions.
facts: High-altitude lake near Tawang–Bum La route
Part of local sacred lake circuit
Access subject to permits and weather

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main town of Tawang at about 2,700–3,000 m elevation, gateway for the monastery, passes, and lakes. Monpa cultural hub with markets, hotels, and base for exploring the region; requires Inner Line Permit.
facts: Base for Tawang Monastery and circuits
